source_note: RxNav's live Drug-Drug Interaction API was permanently discontinued by NLM in Jan 2024. This file is a manually curated rule set based on well-documented, publicly known interactions (ONC High-Priority style pairs), cross-referenced against openFDA label warnings. See README Scope & Limitations.

interaction_rules.description: Combined use significantly increases risk of bleeding due to additive anticoagulant/antiplatelet effects.
NSAIDs increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin; also raises GI bleed risk independently.
Antibiotics can disrupt gut flora that synthesize vitamin K, potentiating warfarin's anticoagulant effect and raising INR.
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, slowing clearance of the S-warfarin isomer and increasing INR and bleeding risk.
Thyroid hormone increases clotting factor turnover, potentiating warfarin's anticoagulant effect; INR should be monitored closely after any dose change.
Statins can mildly potentiate warfarin's anticoagulant effect via CYP interaction; periodic INR monitoring is generally advised.
Ibuprofen competitively blocks aspirin's irreversible binding to COX-1 on platelets, reducing aspirin's cardioprotective antiplatelet effect.
NSAIDs blunt the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and, combined, increase risk of reduced kidney function, especially with volume depletion.
NSAIDs can reduce the antihypertensive effectiveness of beta-blockers through sodium and fluid retention.
Reduced gastric acidity from PPIs impairs levothyroxine absorption; doses should be separated and thyroid function monitored.
ACE inhibitors can modestly increase insulin sensitivity, slightly raising hypoglycemia risk when combined with glucose-lowering agents.
Two antihypertensive agents used together have an additive blood-pressure-lowering effect; monitor for symptomatic hypotension, particularly at treatment initiation.
